### T-509 — Implement the chat orchestration and prompt store

> _2026-10-29 · realm/blong-chat · done_

Add chat.in.message.receive, chat.in.answer.receive, chat.out.message.send, chat.prompt.ask and
chat.prompt.find, with library functions for the account lookup, the pending prompt store and the
forward seams. The ask parks a promise, sends the controls and resolves on the answer or expires
with chatPromptTimeout @@D-678.

chat.in.receive routes to messageReceive, answerReceive or out.promptForm; prompt.ask parks a
promise with a timeout and a store behind three library functions; prompt.find lists what is
waiting. Verified live: chat.prompt.find answered {prompts: []} through the gateway and
chat.out.messageSend reached its handler and refused the missing Viber account with
viber.accountMissing.

### T-510 — Declare the chat gateway validations

> _2026-10-29 · realm/blong-chat · done_

gateway/chat/ declares chat.message.send, chat.prompt.ask and chat.in.answer.receive with auth false
and explicit TypeBox params and results, so a local tool calls them with plain JSON-RPC and a
deployment protects the address instead @@D-682.

Four public validations with auth false: out.messageSend, prompt.ask, prompt.find and
in.answerReceive. Verified over HTTP against a dev run: prompt.find answered without a token, and
the methods whose names end in a word group (messageSend) were the ones whose route needed renaming
after the 401 proved the old dotted name was never registered.

### T-527 — Per-account chat addressing, tunnel manifest and question shapes

> _2026-10-30 · realm/blong-chat · done_

Done in this round: per-account `url`/`ngrokUrl`/`configToken` on `IChatAccount`,
`chatAccountBase`/`chatPublicUrl` shared by both ports, every Slack and Viber descriptor carrying
its account's base, `chat.chatDispatch.forward` as a map with a `*` fallback (the old string shape
still read as `*`), the gateway accepting positional params, radio buttons plus a free-text box in
the Slack modal when a placeholder is given, `CHAT_TEST_PORT` moving every test address at once, and
the docs (README, chat.http, blong_devrc.example) showing the three question shapes and the tunnel
setup. The tunnel is discovered rather than configured: `ngrokPublicUrl` picks the tunnel whose
`config.addr` names the listener's port from the agent's `api/tunnels`, and
`ngrokUrl`/`ngrokAgentUrl` are overrides.

### T-528 — Replace the controls once the question is answered

> _2026-10-30 · realm/blong-chat · done_

The answer is now echoed as a follow-up message (`@@D-690`), so the record exists, but the question
message itself is still left as it was: the choice buttons or the "answer" form button stay in the
channel, and the controls still invite a click that can no longer do anything. The remaining work is
to replace them once `chat.prompt.answer` resolves — `chat.update` for the Slack message, or the
payload's `response_url` with `replace_original`, and an edit or a replacement message for Viber's
keyboard — which needs the receiver to map `response_url` and the message `ts` onto `IChatInbound`
and the outbound port to accept them. That widening is why it is still open: the echo needed none of
it.

The question message is now rewritten once it is answered — options kept and marked, controls gone
(`@@D-692`).
